https://www.barrons.com/articles/apple-spreading-augmented-reality-says-rosenblatt-homepod-struggles-1521216592 Apple Spreading Augmented Reality, Says Rosenblatt; HomePod Struggles By March 16, 2018 12:09 p.m. ET Text Size Medium Large Apple's bringing its augmented reality sensors to more models of the iPhone later this year, according to a report from analyst Jun Zhang of the boutique research house Rosenblatt Securities / Credit: Tiernan Ray for Barron's. 
Apple ( AAPL ) is bringing augmented reality to more of its iPhone s, and also to the iPad , according to a report this morning from Rosenblatt ’s Jun Zhang , who relates comments from his unnamed supply-chain sources. 
The company will with the next iPhone “cycle” — presumably this fall — produce a 6.1-inch iPhone model that has an LCD screen, rather than the OLED screen of the current iPhone X, and a front-facing camera with a 3-D sensing design akin to the “ True Depth ” camera on the iPhone X that makes possible the “Face ID” feature. 
Zhang, who has a Buy rating on Apple shares, and a $180 price target, is hearing Apple’s rumored larger iPhone , perhaps a 6.5-inch OLED model, "will very likely add a dual-SIM design for some markets differentiating this model from the 5.8 and 6.1-inch models.” It may also come in a gold finish to further make this model stand apart from the lower-priced versions, he writes. 
Zhang writes that the iPad Pro may gain the True Depth camera, perhaps via "a larger dot projector with increased VCSEL content." 
However, it will be at least another year before augmented reality comes to the rear camera of the iPhone, he believes. 
He also muses that Apple may enlist Sony ( SNE ) for "a multi-array TOF [time of flight]" camera system for the rear of the iPhone, which he thinks could come with 2019’s iPhone models. 
"We note that overheating and battery consumption are two bottlenecks for multi-array ToF adoption in the rear camera,” writes Zhang. 
Zhang warns that Q2 production for iPhone is being reduced, writing “there may have been reductions in Q2 component order cuts among Apple supply chain participants." 
He sees that as a risk to multiple Apple suppliers, including Synaptics ( SYNA ), Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ), Knowles ( KN ), Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ), Qorvo ( QRVO ), and Universal Display ( OLED ). 
He also trims his estimates for Apple’s recently released HomePod speaker, now projecting 3 million units to be sold this year, half what he was expecting previously. 
“We have seen weaker than expected sales” of HomePod, he writes. 
Zhang offers the hope that “the low-cost HomePod model could see better traction due to competitive pricing against Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ’s ( GOOGL ),” assuming Apple were to put on sale a cheaper model with "a timely launch time before the holiday season." 
Apple shares today are down 77 cents at $177.89, while shares of suppliers are all going higher, with Cirrus up $2, or 4.6%, at $45.06, and Universal Display up 35 cents at $123.90.
